claim: Schools running multiple students through a single shared NAT hit IP-based rate limits on cloud AI tools with errors like 'too many sessions from 1 IP', and vendors offer no easy whitelisting channel.
quote: our students go to chatgpt on their own account, but through the school network and thereby use one of our 3 connections... There is no way to contact anybody from support directly

claim: Lovable's free plan gives only 5 daily credits resetting at midnight UTC, capped at 30/month — exhausted after roughly 3 meaningful prompts, which makes the free tier insufficient for a 2-3 hour workshop without upgrades.
quote: 5 daily credits ... up to a maximum of 30 per month. Daily credits are being reset every day at midnight UTC.

claim: Non-coders hit immediate paywalls and broken outputs on first-touch with vibe-coding tools: Cursor required a $20 Pro subscription up front and still failed, Replit produced broken layouts, and Bolt shipped missing nav links.
quote: After connecting my GitHub account and entering my prompt, I was met with a paywall ... After an hour of frustration and $20 down the drain, I had to give up

claim: Lovable has logged 314+ outages since May 2025, with recent incidents lasting from 15 minutes to 10+ hours — so any single-tool workshop on a launch-surge day risks losing the whole session.
quote: StatusGator has been monitoring Lovable outages, downtime, and service disruptions ... more than 314 outages that affected Lovable users ... Empty chat views in projects ... 10h 15m

claim: Workshop facilitators recommend frequent git commits and a pre-built starter template (e.g. McKay Wrigley's full-stack scaffold) so participants can pin bugs to a commit and the LLM can recover faster.
quote: commit your code frequently. If I can pinpoint exactly which commit introduced a bug, the LLM does a much better job at solving the problem.

claim: Multi-host vibe-coding workshops in 2025-2026 consistently surface 'tool flexibility' — stay ready to swap models/platforms mid-session — as a top takeaway, implying a documented backup-tool requirement.
quote: staying flexible and adaptable by exploring various models and platforms

claim: Cursor's student verification via SheerID throws a 'Verification Limit Exceeded' error when many participants from the same school domain sign up in a short window, with a 72-hour cooldown that can kill a workshop.
quote: We're glad you're enthusiastic, but it looks like you've already redeemed or attempted to redeem this offer ... SheerID's system resets every 72 hours

claim: Claude requires SMS phone verification at account creation, meaning workshop attendees without a phone (or with VOIP numbers) can be blocked from signing up at the door.
quote: asked to enter their phone number from a supported location to receive a verification code via text message

claim: Experienced classroom hosts treat a phone mobile-hotspot as the standard wifi-failure backup, with pay-as-you-go cellular data the recommended low-budget plan B.
quote: a hotspot is a perfect backup plan for teaching ... the ability to use the data on your phone on your computer or iPad

claim: Cross-host post-mortems agree that beautiful prototypes from vibe-coding sessions fall apart under real testing unless facilitators force a planning step before participants start prompting.
quote: Vibe coding is a communication and exploration tool, not a shortcut past the thinking ... Skipped steps, fast execution — beautiful prototypes nobody needs.

claim: A facilitator who has run multiple AI prototyping workshops settled on Lovable as her default classroom tool after starting with Bolt and v0, citing lower friction for non-technical participants.
quote: Lovable has become her default workshop tool, and in her very first AI prototyping workshop she used Bolt
